commitResults.messageTitle: Fix loop boolean name to fit convention
Made the project into a package
Add command list on startup and bye closes
Refactor command-line workflow into focused methods
commitResults.messageBody: The command-line entry point mixed menu display, input validation, task construction, persistence, and command routing in one deeply nested method. Splitting those responsibilities into named methods keeps each step at a consistent abstraction level, makes the happy path easier to follow, and removes comments that merely narrated the implementation.

Parsing only the first character made unrelated inputs such as '10' and 'q anything' look valid. Validating the complete command makes the accepted forms explicit while preserving the documented list-search suffix.

Echo mode read input unconditionally, so closing the input stream caused an exception instead of a normal shutdown. Checking availability before reading makes the exceptional path explicit and lets the surrounding command-line session exit cleanly.

Several older classes used two-space indentation, overlong statements, misaligned switch labels, vague date names, and narration-style comments. Consistent formatting and explanatory names reduce visual surprises, while final fields and a non-instantiable constants class make their intended roles explicit.

Raw numeric indexes and record lengths obscured the meaning of persisted task fields. Named constants, descriptive local variables, and focused construction helpers make the file format visible in the code and keep record parsing at one level of abstraction.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract the shared task search predicate
commitResults.messageBody: The GUI and command-line list flows duplicated the same case-insensitive matching expression. Giving that rule one descriptive boolean method removes duplication and lets both loops state their intent directly.
The constructor comment described a file-path parameter that does not exist. Documenting the actual default-file behavior prevents the API comment from contradicting the code and tripping up readers.

Rambo duplicated TaskList's one-based index conversion and bounds validation when retrieving tasks. Exposing one validated lookup operation removes that duplication and keeps ownership of list indexing inside TaskList.

The GUI dispatcher repeated keyword checks and substring extraction in a long method, obscuring the command-to-operation mapping. Split the keyword from its arguments once and use focused dispatch methods with explicit default branches, following the code-quality guidance on short methods and duplication.

Preserve command syntax, case handling, aliases, and error responses. Add regression coverage for these boundaries; all 65 tests pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share task addition and persistence across interfaces
commitResults.messageBody:
Four GUI and CLI task-creation paths repeated the same list mutation and save operation. Extract addAndSaveTask so this behavior has one implementation and future persistence changes cannot leave one creation path behind.

Keep response formatting in each interface and preserve the existing add-then-save order. All 65 tests pass on Java 25.

The controller never reads its sendButton field; FXML invokes handleUserInput directly. Remove the dead field, import, and unused fx:id so readers do not assume the controller needs to manage the button.

The button and its action remain intact. Verified the FXML is well-formed and the Java 25 build passes all 65 tests.

Replace inline window-size and message-spacing numbers with named constants so their purpose is explicit and layout settings are easy to locate, following the guideline to avoid magic numbers. Document the window startup method while clarifying its layout configuration.

Retain every existing dimension. The Java 25 build and all 65 tests pass.

Parser and Task each define the same priority-range check and error
message. Keeping two copies makes it easy for accepted input and task
updates to disagree when the priority rules change.

Extract the shared check into Task.validatePriorityLevel and call it
from both entry points.

Keep the rule with Task because it also applies to updates that bypass
user-input parsing, including loading saved tasks. Leave numeric text
conversion in Parser so its input-specific error remains unchanged.

All 65 tests pass on Java 25, including priority boundary tests for the
parser, task model, and storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Guard task records before reading their fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage reads the task-type field before checking whether any fields
exist. A record containing only separators produces an empty array and
raises ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of RamboException.

This bypasses the application's normal invalid-record error handling
and hides the offending record from the user.

Reject records shorter than the minimum task record before accessing
their fields. Add regression coverage for separator-only records.

An early guard keeps malformed input handling ahead of task creation
and reuses the existing invalid-record message. Retain the per-type
field-count checks for deadline and event records.

The regression test reproduces the failure before the fix. All 66 tests
pass on Java 25 after the fix, including legacy-format loading tests.

Storage uses loops to skip blank records, convert tasks to saved text,
and trim record fields. These loops mix the intended transformations
with collection updates and index management.

Replace the three loops with stream filtering and mapping operations.

The pipelines make each transformation explicit while preserving task
order, blank-line handling, and invalid-record errors. Collect loaded
tasks into an ArrayList to retain the mutable return value.

All 66 tests pass on Java 25 with these changes.
